scope: Pre-execution mathematical and measurement review; not an exhaustive literature audit or experiment result.
source_policy: Original source.yaml and normalized record fields remain unchanged. Notes are separate proposed corrections.

findings.finding: For a nonconstant j-map of degree D, the image of M smooth rational parameters has at least ceil(M/D) j-values. If D=O(chi) and M=p-O(chi), image density is Omega(1/chi), not O(chi/p). Constant-j and p-growing-degree families must be separate strata.
findings.action: Replace the claimed density obstruction by measured image sizes, j-map degree, and fibre-isomorphism-class coverage; keep the high-rank prescribed-fibre question open.

findings.finding: For y^2=x^3+A x+B, the twist has coefficients f^2 A,f^3 B and discriminant f^6 Delta. A simple zero of f=(t-t0)g at a good target fibre creates bad reduction, rather than changing the twist class of that smooth fibre.
findings.action: Require f(t0) nonzero, prescribe its square class, and check minimal-model good reduction. Twists preserve j.

findings.basis: primary source and cohomological degree bound
findings.finding: Ulmer proves Tate/BSD for particular families, not every random elliptic surface. With chi=3 the second Betti number is 34, so ten power sums do not generically determine its Frobenius polynomial. Distinguish arithmetic rank over F_p(t) from geometric rank over the algebraic closure.
findings.action: Specify the valid Tate theorem or conditional rank label per family, a sufficient Frobenius reconstruction algorithm, and independently certified sections and rank bounds.

findings.finding: The 2 chi upper bound applies to sections disjoint from O. A shortest nonzero section need not be disjoint from O; rank zero has no lambda_1.
findings.action: State the section condition and height convention; measure shortest heights only for positive certified rank.

findings.finding: Finding a section does not supply its coordinates in a certified MW basis. r sections through O need not give r independent kernel relations, nor a full-index kernel lattice. The reduced generators may span a proper subgroup of the fibre.
findings.action: Include basis-coordinate recovery, torsion and saturation, relation independence/index certificates, target-subgroup coverage, and matrix solvability modulo the chosen subgroup order in completed-operation timing. Separate oracle-assisted and blind measurements.

findings.finding: General sections have rational-function coordinates and can specialize to O through poles. Polynomial x(t),y(t) alone miss these sections. The asserted coefficient count, height-to-degree conversion, and uniqueness are not defined by canonical height alone.
findings.action: Specify a projective or denominator-inclusive parametrization, degree bounds, normalization, denominator saturation, O-fibre constraints, and the exact random-system control. Do not claim exactly one solution from the Gaussian heuristic.

findings.finding: Use H as squared norm, G as its Gram matrix, and N(H) approximately V_r H^(r/2)/sqrt(det G). lambda_1 alone does not determine det G or coverage. At r=100, p=2^256, G=18 I, the exact-volume heuristic gives H approximately 3882; this illustrative lattice is not an E1 measurement.
findings.action: Record G, determinant, covolume, torsion, and lambda_1 conventions explicitly. Derive d and unknown counts from the E3 encoding. Treat N>=p as a necessary count, not a surjectivity certificate.

findings.finding: For A4, none of n in {31,61,89,127} is divisible by d in {2,3,5}, so the stated integer digit k=n/d and ring map are unavailable for every listed pair. F1 likewise needs d dividing n and a degree-d irreducible defining polynomial.
findings.action: Choose compatible exponents and primes; verify alpha maps to an actual root modulo p, the field degree, and a good degree-one reduction prime. Normalize closure by |D|/#E(F_p).

findings.finding: At subgroup order near 2^32, the expected nonzero kernel hits in the prescribed box are about 8.66e-7, 5.28e-5, and 0.00322 at ranks 2,3,4. The origin supplies no independent relation. HNF cannot certify the full kernel from an insufficient zero set; unpowered MI tests cannot support independence.
findings.action: Precompute expected hits and power; use smaller synthetic subgroups or larger/conditional samples with sampling-bias controls. Report unknown when index reconstruction or independence cannot be resolved. Exclude bad reduction primes and define smoothness of signed rational net values, including zeros.

findings.finding: The stated m^r |F| coverage bound implies r >= log(p/|F|)/log(m) for full coverage, rather than log(p)/log(m) unless |F| is constant. Quantitative thresholds also depend on m, factor-base size, determinant, target coverage, and the constant in L_p(1/2).
findings.action: Parameterize these quantities. Distinguish certified independent generators of a sublattice from a saturated full MW basis; restrict lattice enumeration to an explicit finite workload.

findings.finding: A generic Q(s) rank bound does not bound ranks of all specialized Q-curves. A uniform generator-height lower bound c log p is false for lifts of a fixed small-coefficient rational curve as p varies. Lang-style bounds need their exact hypotheses and conjectural status.
findings.action: Keep rank and height distributions empirical for the stated ensembles; remove the generic-surface inference about all specializations. Supply discriminant, minimal model, height constants, rank certificates, and certificate provenance for reused rank-campaign curves.

findings.finding: The rank of zero apparition is ord(P), but the full EDS value period can be larger. The equivalence theorem concerns specified EDS problems and does not itself establish the asserted linear-complexity profile.
findings.action: Record zero-apparition rank, value period, and normalization separately. Budget sequence length and Berlekamp-Massey memory before attempting L near ten times a 40-bit order; a five-hour estimate is not a demonstrated bound.

findings.finding: For good reduction, [N]Qtilde lies in the formal group and its logarithm is in p Z_p. If p does not divide N, log([N]Qtilde)/N mod p is identically zero, not a uniform statistic on F_p.
findings.action: If lift randomness is to be measured, define the rescaled statistic with its p factor, lift distribution, precision, and information estimator. A splitting statement is relative to one fixed curve lift, and the anomalous control must distinguish random from canonical curve lifts.

findings.finding: A root of H_D is not by itself a complete canonical-lift certificate for an arbitrary finite-field model. The endomorphism order, selected local root, twist/model, and precision must match.
findings.action: Certify End(E), H_D-root selection, reduction isomorphism and lifted endomorphisms; restrict Hensel/Newton to hypotheses where the algorithm is valid.

findings.finding: Changing a lift in a multiplicative extension changes its N-multiple coordinate by an Nth power, so the natural target is F_q^*/(F_q^*)^N before reduction. Divisibility l | q-1 permits a nontrivial pairing, but does not ensure a chosen extension class pairs nontrivially.
findings.action: Specify quotient, reduced-pairing convention, admissible class, argument domains and nondegeneracy controls before comparing Miller values.

findings.finding: The standard L(1/3) constants use cube roots: (32/9)^(1/3) and (64/9)^(1/3), not the raw fractions. Computing embedding orders requires factorization/certification costs. Raw k distributions across varying subgroup orders need a normalization.
findings.action: Define k/l or another comparable statistic, include curve-count/factorization/order-certificate costs, and fix Murphy-E region and optimization budget. Enforce the explicit no-sieving rule; public-parameter arithmetic remains separate from toy ECDLP operations.

findings.finding: Chevalley's structure theorem identifies an affine subgroup and an abelian quotient; an arbitrary surjection to E can also have an abelian kernel. This classification alone is not a general computational lower bound or proof that all conceivable transfers have been excluded.
findings.action: Restrict the receipt to the specified generalized Jacobians, define k from residue degrees, and give the exact group-extension argument. Replace full modulus enumeration with a justified bounded enumeration or symbolic classification and verify its size.

findings.basis: dimension does not bound unrestricted finite conditions
findings.finding: An algebraic condition on E may select a zero-dimensional set. Hasse-Weil requires hypotheses on components and genus; it does not establish the stated universal description-size or genus lower bound for all factor bases.
findings.action: Restrict to explicit bounded-complexity absolutely irreducible cover families and supply the image/fibre-count argument. Preserve the claimed general obstruction as unverified, rather than issuing a theorem receipt for it.

findings.basis: algorithmic upper bound is not a lower bound
findings.finding: A cost estimate for a named genus-g index-calculus algorithm is not a lower bound for every algorithm on the E-component. Rho is still available on that component. Some cover maps have finite kernels on rational points, so 'inside' needs a precise map.
findings.action: Scope the receipt and exponent fits to the named algorithm and family; certify cover/isogeny maps and E-component membership. Do not label universal impossibility or absence of crossover as theorem-closed.

findings.finding: Write disc(Z[pi])=t^2-4p=f_pi^2 D_K and disc End(E)=f_E^2 D_K with f_E dividing f_pi. Division by f^2 is correct only when f denotes [End(E):Z[pi]]. H_D has degree h(D), whereas its ring class field has degree h(D) over the quadratic field and 2h(D) over Q.
findings.action: Define f and the global field in each measurement. Treat typical sqrt(p) growth and rational-height statistics as empirical distribution claims, allowing small-CM and rational-j exceptions; do not infer a universal lower bound on local approximation or on all canonical-lift algorithms.

findings.finding: Multiplicativity of Teichmueller lifts does not prove Dickman-distributed smoothness or absence of bias among their sparse truncated representatives.
findings.action: Keep the algebraic identity receipt-only and label the smoothness comparison a heuristic finite measurement, with expected event counts and uncertainty bounds.

findings.finding: A universal integer polynomial is independent of the chosen prime, but specialization and reduction can erase coefficients or alter factorization. No identity proves a <=3x solver-throughput bound.
findings.action: Separate a symbolic identity receipt from empirical support, factorization, and timing observations; exclude or explicitly record exceptional coefficient reductions.

findings.finding: |F|^m/(m! #E) estimates a relation count, not an unbounded probability; the stated expression exceeds one for some grid cells. Enumeration cost differs between two-sum and three-sum searches and between planted and random targets.
findings.action: Measure actual factor-base cardinality, relation multiplicities, saturated target yield, full target search costs, and a matched enumeration baseline for each m. Fit exponents with uncertainty and censored-timeout handling; a three-size fit is not an asymptotic result.

findings.finding: A success in one planted toy instance or an inferred threshold at one bit size does not establish the required relation-search cost or a usable factor base. A generic linear bivariate modular equation is not a uniquely specified validation control.
findings.action: Specify the exact control polynomial, proven range, lattice basis/parameters and threshold estimator with confidence intervals. Fix sweep direction and censored cases before running; include planting and all solver costs separately.

findings.finding: A floating height-pairing determinant alone does not certify exact dependence or the size of every integer relation. Fitting three or four points needs a specified family and sampling law.
findings.action: Define the fit construction, exclude duplicates and torsion as intended, recover exact integer relations, verify them in E(Q), and report certified rank intervals where rank is unresolved.

findings.finding: Several grids write p=2^n, which is not a prime; interpret these as bit-size placeholders only after an explicit prime-selection rule is recorded. Multiple proposed enumeration workloads and high-dimensional lattices lack demonstrated feasibility within their estimates. Source names and novelty assertions are provisional, not verified bibliographic evidence.
findings.action: Record actual certified primes, nonsingular curves, independent replicate seeds, immutable solver builds, operation boundaries, CPU/RAM caps, timeouts and censoring. Confirm external certificates and tool availability. Archive hypotheses separately from evidence, preserve theorem-receipt-only restrictions, and keep toy/public-parameter branches distinct.
